jurisdiction: United States independent-agency research pilot; licensing, appointment, privacy and state filing requirements require agency-specific review.
source_frame: Action Model system-map industry slug insurance_agencies; taxonomy reference only, not demand or implementation proof.
scope_note: This record concerns agency-side intake, service and renewal administration. Carriers retain underwriting, claims and policy authority; an agency workflow may prepare or route information but cannot bind coverage, decide a claim or replace a licensed producer.
summary: Start with supervised submission intake, document completeness, certificate/service requests and renewal preparation. Existing agency-management products already advertise broad workflow capabilities, so any pilot must compare against the actual incumbent and preserve carrier and licensed-producer authority.

automation_research.finding: BLS describes insurance-sales-agent work that includes interviewing applicants, explaining policies and contacting existing policyholders. That task inventory supports measuring administrative assistance around collection, reminders and document preparation; it does not establish an automation rate, carrier acceptance or permission to make coverage decisions.
automation_research.forecast_note: No independently measured agency automation percentage or adoption rate is used. Vendor feature pages are capability evidence only, not realized savings or prevalence evidence.

modules.capability: Schema-driven forms and structured responses useful for supervised applicant or service-request intake.
modules.reuse_shape: Version-pinned intake component with SISO-owned schemas, consent, response storage and export; no automatic coverage recommendation or bind action.
modules.rights_state: GitHub metadata and project licensing require route-specific review before adoption.
modules.limits: Form capability does not prove accessibility, carrier integration, consent sufficiency, licensing compliance or field-level validation for a particular line of business.

modules.capability: Reusable connectors and event-driven workflow execution for reminders, routing and approved back-office actions.
modules.reuse_shape: Allowlisted draft/notification flows with explicit producer approval for carrier-facing or client-facing writes.
modules.rights_state: Project README distinguishes community and enterprise boundaries; license and connector route need review.
modules.limits: Connectors do not prove carrier API permission, idempotency, retry safety, secrets handling or producer authority.

modules.capability: Read-oriented dashboards and queries for governed service, renewal and exception metrics.
modules.reuse_shape: Separate read model for operational reporting; never the policy, premium, claims or accounting system of record.
modules.rights_state: Project edition and embedding/license route require review before client-facing use.
modules.limits: Dashboards do not establish data freshness, metric correctness, tenant isolation or permission to expose protected client information.

processes.process: New-business submission intake and completeness chase
processes.automation_boundary: Collect supplied applicant and risk fields, normalize documents and flag missing or inconsistent items; do not recommend coverage, bind or represent carrier acceptance.
processes.baseline_required: Matched submission volume, completeness/error rate, human minutes including chase and review, actual software spend and operator cost.
processes.metric: Human minutes per complete, producer-accepted submission, including review, rework and exceptions
processes.falsifier: Reject if missing or conflicting risk facts are silently accepted, unauthorized data is exposed, or total reviewed human effort does not decrease.
processes.human_authority: Licensed producer or designated agency reviewer decides whether a submission is complete and suitable to send; carrier decides underwriting and acceptance.

processes.process: Policy-service request triage and document preparation
processes.automation_boundary: Classify incoming service requests, locate policy context and draft a checklist or response for review; do not alter policy terms or issue an endorsement automatically.
processes.baseline_required: Matched request volume and class, first-response quality, human minutes including escalations/rework, actual spend and operator cost.
processes.metric: Net human minutes per correctly routed and producer-approved request, including exceptions and reopenings
processes.falsifier: Reject if a request is routed to the wrong client/policy, stale information is sent, or an external write occurs without approval.
processes.human_authority: Agency service owner and licensed producer retain authority over advice, policy changes and carrier communication.

processes.automation_boundary: Gather request facts and prepare a draft from verified policy records; require an authorized reviewer before release and never infer coverage beyond the policy.
processes.baseline_required: Matched certificate volume, turnaround, correction/reissue rate, human minutes including review, actual spend and operator cost.
processes.metric: Human minutes per accurate, authorized certificate, with corrections, exceptions and recipient verification counted
processes.falsifier: Reject if a certificate states unsupported coverage, goes to an unauthorized recipient, or review/reissue effort offsets the time reduction.
processes.human_authority: Authorized agency staff verifies policy facts and recipient before release; the certificate does not amend policy or create carrier authority.

processes.automation_boundary: Surface upcoming expirations, missing renewal information and changed fields for producer review; do not select limits, recommend replacement coverage or bind renewal.
processes.baseline_required: Matched renewal volume, on-time completion, exception/rework rate, human minutes including producer review, actual spend and operator cost.
processes.metric: Human minutes per on-time, producer-approved renewal packet; missed deadlines, exceptions and rework
processes.falsifier: Reject if stale or incomplete records suppress a renewal exception, a recommendation is presented as fact, or producer review does not reduce net effort.
processes.human_authority: Licensed producer owns coverage comparison, recommendation and renewal/bind decision; carrier owns underwriting and issuance.

observed_business_value.reason: No agency baseline, invoices, achieved automation rate, review/rework measurement, operating cost, realized cash savings or eligible-population measurement was verified. Null is not zero.

pilot.design: Within one authorized independent agency, compare matched redacted or synthetic submissions, service requests, certificates and renewals under the incumbent and supervised candidate workflows. Pre-register authority boundaries and rollback conditions before live data.
record: assisted human minutes including review and rework
reject_if: Human effort including review and rework is not lower than the matched baseline.
Any policy, client or carrier data crosses an unauthorized boundary or an unapproved external write occurs.
A draft, reminder or extracted field is treated as a coverage decision, bind, claim decision or carrier acceptance.
Measured first-year net cash is not positive for a cash-savings offer; capacity gains alone are not cash.

limitations: This is not insurance, legal, underwriting, claims or financial advice, product admission or an industry-wide value forecast.
Independent-agency software adoption, prices, carrier acceptance and realized savings were not verified; named offerings are not assumed installed.
Carrier-versus-agency authority, producer licensing, state rules, privacy/security, accessibility and retention need agency-specific review.
No generic repository is treated as a replacement for an agency-management system, policy system of record or carrier portal.
Applied Systems agency-management URL returned HTTP 521 on the independent parent recheck; do not infer fresh capability or availability from that failure.
